findings.claim: Requirement says all generated code should be decorated, but the change emits the attribute only for non-netstandard2.0 and non-.NET Framework targets, so those targets are unmarked. This is deliberate per [L12], which records no preference and says to follow the requirement. The README documents the limitation.

receipt_plan.detail: [L12] asked whether netstandard2.0/.NET Framework output should also be excluded and answered 'No preference; follow the requirement'. The conditional emission is therefore not a defect.

findings.claim: The change modifies the runtime decimal formatter to write with StandardFormat 'F'. This is unrelated to the code-coverage requirement and alters serialized bytes. It is a wire-format change hidden in a coverage PR. [L8] records that numeric serialization is bug-prone. Decimal output for values like 1E-10 would change, and the change has no tests or docs for it.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize decimals such as 1E-10, 1.0m, 79228162514264337593543950335m and 0.0000000000000000000000000001m with base-built and head-built MessagePack; compare bytes and check the round trip.

findings.claim: The TransformUtilities change alters the output whitespace for nesting types with constraints ('{' becomes '{\r\n'). It is unrelated to the requirement and has no explanation. It changes the snapshots of generated files for constrained nested generics, beyond adding the attribute.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests and inspect the snapshot diffs for nested constrained generic types, checking for changes beyond the attribute lines.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no-setting reading. Every generated formatter and resolver type, including the nested FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper types, gets the attribute inside an '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' guard in the .tt templates and the generated .cs files. No opt-out option exists.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Opt-out reading. The same attribute is emitted by default, but a new generator option (for example an MSBuild property or a GeneratedMessagePackResolver/assembly attribute property) disables emission. The templates read that option and emit the attribute only when it is enabled. The attribute would also be available on netstandard2.0 through a generated internal attribute definition or an existence check.
